messages:
Maya: heads-up — multiple customers reporting streaming responses aborting with what looks like server 5xx spikes. started seeing this ~2h ago.

Alejandra: saw support tickets — customers show client-side errors like "broken pipe" and our dashboard shows an uptick in 5xx for /v1/streams. they think the stream died mid-response and we incremented a 5xx.

Tom: can you paste an example log? is it EPIPE or chunked encoding failure?

Alejandra: pasted from customer log: 
```
2024-10-21T14:12:05Z gateway: upstream write failed: write tcp 10.10.0.5:443->10.2.1.9:34512: write: broken pipe
2024-10-21T14:12:05Z router: proxy error: chunked encoding failed while writing body
```
They also attached our access log showing status=502 for the same request.

Liam: interesting — if the client disconnects while we're streaming, some gateways (nginx/envoy/our proxy) surface that as a 5xx in upstream metrics. nginx would report 499 (client closed), but depending on where the socket closed we get EPIPE on write and the gateway decides.

Maya: customer claim: client is closing connection on receipt of certain control-chunk; but we should not be counting that as our server failure. that inflates error rates and triggers paging.

eng-runtime-oncall: tagging in. we should triage as: 1) repro locally 2) inspect gateway mapping of EPIPE/ECONNRESET -> status counters 3) short-term mitigation to stop paging.

Tom: repro notes from my end — I created a small Node script that connects to /v1/streams and closes after receiving first chunk. it reliably causes gateway to log EPIPE and increments 5xx counter. here's the repro script (quick):
```
// client-disconnect.js
const http = require('http');
const req = http.request({ host: 'api.redwood.example', path: '/v1/streams', method: 'POST' }, res => {
  res.on('data', chunk => {
    console.log('got chunk');
    req.abort(); // simulate client disconnect
  });
});
req.end(JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'hi' }));
```
Run w/ curl too: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams` then ctrl-c after first frame — same effect.

Liam: thanks. server stack: our streaming handler writes chunked frames and keeps connection open while model generates. when the socket write returns EPIPE it bubbles up. gateway currently maps these to 502/504 in metrics because upstream abruptly closed. we need to classify them separately.

eng-runtime-oncall: short term: patch metrics layer to detect EPIPE/ECONNRESET and increment 499-like counter instead of 5xx. low-risk hotfix to avoid alerting. i'll open a small PR to metric-router to map errno->status bucket.

Maya: can we also expose in tenant metrics a count of aborted streams vs server failures? customers keep complaining about our SLA.

eng-runtime-oncall: yes — add a tag `aborted_client_disconnect=true` on those spans and a metric `stream.client_aborts`. will add to PR.

Alejandra: what about customers behind proxies (Cloudflare, corp proxies) that terminate poorly? any client advice?

Tom: advise: prefer graceful stream close (SSE: dispatch event type done; websockets: send final frame then close) rather than hard TCP close. Also set `Connection: keep-alive` and avoid middleboxes that timeout short. If they must close early, it's a client abort and our system shouldn't be penalized.

Liam: longer-term: gateway tweaks — tune keepalive, disable buffering for /v1/streams route (nginx proxy_buffering off) so our writes pass through immediately. for Envoy we can set `disable_chunk_encoding=false`? (need to double-check flag) — but main point is don't let intermediate buffer convert a client disconnect into upstream write-time error that counts as server error.

Maya: any quick mitigation we can tell the paging policy to do? right now SRE gets paged at 90th percentile 5xx spike.

eng-runtime-oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) exclude route /v1/streams from SLO-based alerting for the next 24h while we patch metrics; 2) route count change — reduce sensitivity on that alert; 3) apply hotfix to categorize EPIPE as non-5xx. I'll coordinate with SRE to suppress pages.

Alejandra: can you share the PR link and we can tell impacted customers ETA?

eng-runtime-oncall: PR: https://git.redwood/inference/metric-router/pull/942 (WIP) — ETA 3h for rollout to canary, 8h full roll. will post updates.

Tom: spike note — also saw a different class of failures where chunked encoding headers were malformed by corp proxy and our parser returned 500. those are actual server errors and we'll keep counting them. need to distinguish.

Liam: actionable checklist: 
- [ ] reproduce & attach minimal repro (Tom done)
- [ ] map errno->metric bucket hotfix (eng-runtime-oncall)
- [ ] add `stream.client_aborts` metric and span tag (eng-runtime-oncall)
- [ ] turn off buffering for streaming route in gateway config (Liam/Tom)
- [ ] document client best-practices for streaming (Alejandra)
- [ ] notify customers and suppress paging (Maya/Alejandra/SRE)

Maya: i'll draft a short customer message: apologize, explain it's client disconnects being miscounted, we are rolling a fix to avoid false 5xx and provide mitigations.

Alejandra: sample customer note (short):
```
Hi — we're seeing client disconnections on streaming responses that our gateway mistakenly counted as server errors. We're rolling a fix to stop counting these as 5xx and will share ETA. In the meantime, if you can close streams gracefully or use `curl -N` semantics, it avoids surprising gateway termination. Sorry for the noise.
```

eng-runtime-oncall: update — canary deployed. initial telem shows `stream.client_aborts` spiked in same window and 5xx rate for /v1/streams dropped ~85% on canary. rolling to prod in 2h.

Maya: great. after prod rollout let's update runbooks so oncall doesn't have to page for client-abort spikes. also add a note to product that dashboards should separate aborted streams from real 5xx for SLA reporting.

Tom: filing followup ticket to audit other endpoints that stream (embeddings streaming experiments) for similar behavior.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-3312 — Streaming client-abort misclassified as 5xx. Severity: P2. Links: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2024-3312

Liam: thanks team — will post postmortem link here once we complete the full RCA and mitigation timeline.

Maya: closing the support thread for now — will reopen if customers report after rollout. :thumbsup:
